  36+ 0000              ;-- LL28+4              Skips the A >= Q check and always returns with C flag cleared, so this can be called if we know the division will work
  37+ 0000              ;-- LL31                Skips the A >= Q check and does not set the R counter, so this can be used for jumping straight into the division loop if R is already set to 254 and we know the division will work

  46+ 0000 ~                                        ld      c,(hl)                  ; using c as Q var
  47+ 0000 ~                                        cp      c
  48+ 0000 ~                                        FlipCarryFlag
  49+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL2_6502    ; BCS LL2                \ so jump to LL2 to return 255
  50+ 0000 ~                                        ld      b,$FE                   ; LDX #%11111110         \ Set R to have bits 1-7 set, so we can rotate through 7 loop iterations, getting a 1 each time, and then we use b as Rvar

  52+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL29_6502             ; BCS LL29               \ If bit 7 of A was set, then jump straight to the subtraction
  53+ 0000 ~                                        FlipCarryFlag                   ;                          If A < N, then C flag is set.
  54+ 0000 ~                                        JumpIfALTNusng c, prefix1?_LL31_SKIPSUB_6502 ; CMP Q              \ If A < Q, skip the following subtraction
  55+ 0000 ~                                                                            ; BCC P%+4

  57+ 0000 ~                                        ClearCarryFlag
  58+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL31_SKIPSUB_6502:  FlipCarryFlag
  59+ 0000 ~                                        rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
  60+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL31_6502            ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
  61+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,b

  64+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL29_6502:          sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q

 145+ 0000              ; In XX1510 x1 as a 16-bit coordinate (x1_hi x1_lo)
 146+ 0000              ;    XX1532 y1 as a 16-bit coordinate (y1_hi y1_lo)
 147+ 0000              ;    XX12p2 The line's gradient * 256 (so 1.0 = 256)
 148+ 0000              ;    XX12p3 The direction of slope: * Positive = top left to bottom right * Negative (bit 7 set) = top right to bottom left
 149+ 0000              ;    T      The gradient of slope:* 0 if it's a shallow slope * &FF if it's a steep slope
 150+ 0000              ;  Out  XX150               x1 as an 8-bit coordinate
 151+ 0000              ;       XX152               y1 as an 8-bit coordinate
 152+ 0000              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 153+ 0000
 154+ 0000
 155+ 0000              ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 156+ 0000              ;--  Calculate the following:
 157+ 0000              ;--   * If T = 0, this is a shallow slope, so calculate (Y X) = (S x1_lo) * XX12+2
 158+ 0000              ;--   * If T <> 0, this is a steep slope, so calculate (Y X) = (S x1_lo) / XX12+2
 159+ 0000              ;-- giving (Y X) the opposite sign to the slope direction in XX12+3.

 161+ 0000              ClippingCodeLL120Macro:     MACRO   prefix1?

 171+ 0000 ~                                        jr      nz,prefix1?_LL121_6502           ;.

 174+ 0000 ~
 175+ 0000 ~                                        IFDEF DEBUG_LL122_DIRECT"

 178+ 0000 ~                                        ENDIF

 521+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,(Svar)                ; LDA S                  \ Store the type of slope in XX12+3, bit 7 clear means
 522+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (prefix1?_XX12p3),a              ; STA XX12+3             \ top left to bottom right, bit 7 set means top right to bottom left
 523+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,( prefix1?_XX13)                ; LDA XX13               \ If XX13 = 0, skip the following instruction
 524+ 0000 ~                                        cp      0                       ; BEQ LL138
 525+ 0000 ~                                        jp      z,prefix1?_LL138_6502            ; .
 526+ 0000 ~                                        jp      p, prefix1?_LLX117_6502          ; If XX13 is positive, it must be 95 (64) as 128 would be negative). This means (x1, y1) is on-screen but (x2, y2) isn't, so we jump
 527+ 0000 ~            ;-- If we get here, XX13 = 0 or 191, so (x1, y1) is off-screen and needs clipping
 528+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL138_6502:          call    prefix1?_LL118_6502              ; JSR LL118              \ Call LL118 to move (x1, y1) along the line onto the screen, i.e. clip the line at the (x1, y1) end
 529+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,( prefix1?_XX13)                ; LDA XX13               \ If XX13 = 0, i.e. (x2, y2) is on-screen, jump down to
 530+ 0000 ~                                        and     a
 531+ 0000 ~                                        jp      p,prefix1?_LL124_6502            ; BPL LL124              \ LL124 to return with a successfully clipped line
 532+ 0000 ~            ;-- If we get here, XX13 = 191 (128) (both coordinates areoff-screen)

 537+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,(prefix1?_XX1532)              ; LDA XX15+2             \ If y1_lo > y-coordinate of the bottom of the screen
 538+ 0000 ~                                        cp      128                     ; CMP #Y*2               \ jump to LL137 to return from the subroutine with the
 539+ 0000 ~                                        jp      nc, prefix1?_LL137_6502          ; BCS LL137              \ C flag set, as the line doesn't fit on-screen
 540+ 0000 ~            ;-- If we get here, XX13 = 95 or 191, and in both cases (x2, y2) is off-screen, so we now need to swap the (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) coordinates around before doing the actual clipping, because we need to clip (x2, y2) but the clipping routine at LL118 only clips (x1, y1)
 541+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LLX117_6502:         ld      hl,( prefix1?_XX1510)             ; LDX XX15               \ Swap x1_lo = x2_lo
 542+ 0000 ~                                        ld      de,( prefix1?_XX1554)

 544+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1554),hl
 545+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,( prefix1?_XX1532)             ; LDX XX15+2             \ Swap y1_lo = y2_lo
 546+ 0000 ~                                        ld      de,( prefix1?_XX1576)
 547+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1532),de
 548+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1576),hl
 549+ 0000 ~                                        call    prefix1?_LL118_6502              ; JSR LL118              \ Call LL118 to move (x1, y1) along the line onto the screen, i.e. clip the line at the (x1, y1) end
 550+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,SWAP
 551+ 0000 ~                                        dec     (hl)                    ; DEC SWAP               \ Set SWAP = &FF to indicate that we just clipped the line at the (x2, y2) end by swapping the coordinates (the DEC does this as we set SWAP to 0 at the start of this subroutine)
 552+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL124_6502:          pop     af                      ; PLA            SP+0    \ Restore Y from the stack so it gets preserved through
 553+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Yreg),a                ; TAY                    \ the call to this subroutine
 554+ 0000 ~                                        call    prefix1?_LL146_6502              ; JMP LL146              \ Jump up to LL146 to move the low bytes of (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) into (X1, Y1) and (X2, Y2), and return from the subroutine with a successfully clipped line
 555+ 0000 ~                                        ret                             ; then exit so we don't pop it twice
 556+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL137_6502:          pop     af                      ; PLA            SP+0    \ Restore Y from the stack so it gets preserved through
 557+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Yreg),a                ; TAY                    \ the call to this subroutine
 558+ 0000 ~                                        SetCarryFlag                    ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag to indicate the clipped line does not fit on-screen
 559+ 0000 ~                                        ret                             ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine

  89+ 0000              ; Sets IYH to sign bits, bit 7 = x, bit 6 = y bit 5 = z
  90+ 0000              SetIYHToSignBits:       MACRO
  91+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_ZSGNOFFSET)   ; get Z sign
  92+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
  93+ 0000 ~                                    srl     a                       ;
  94+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
  95+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_YSGNOFFSET)   ; get Y sign
  96+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
  97+ 0000 ~                                    or      iyh                     ; which moves Z into IYH bit 6
  98+ 0000 ~                                    srl     a                       ;
  99+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
 100+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_XSGNOFFSET)   ; get X sign
 101+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
 102+ 0000 ~                                    or      iyh                     ; which moves Y into IYH bit 6 and Z into IYH bit 5
 103+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
 104+ 0000                                      ENDM

 275+ 6097              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 276+ 6097              ; Laser, once a main loop. Times are 50 Hz frames of FrameCounter16 (the interrupt's count, stopped while paused), so a
 277+ 6097              ; pulse lasts as long however fast the loop runs. Like Z-Police's game clock (clock_step): dt = the frames since the last
 278+ 6097              ; update (at most LaserMaxFrames, so a stall doesn't jump), and each state's end is a frame number, compared by 16 bit
 279+ 6097              ; subtraction so it works across the counter's wrap.
 280+ 6097              ;   LaserReady  fire held (LaserFireHeld, from the front view's keys) starts a burst of CurrLaserPulseRate pulses,
 281+ 6097              ;               or with a rate of 0 a beam
 282+ 6097              ;   LaserOn     a pulse, CurrLaserPulseOnTime frames; a beam stays on while fire is held
 283+ 6097              ;   LaserOff    CurrLaserPulseOffTime frames between a burst's pulses
 284+ 6097              ;   LaserRest   CurrLaserPulseRest frames after a burst (or a beam) before the next
 285+ 6097              ; Out: LaserBeamOn (the sprite), LaserHitDamage (what a ship in the sights takes this loop: a pulse's damage when it
 286+ 6097              ; starts, a beam's for each frame it was on), energy drained and heat added for each frame on, the gun cooled for each
 287+ 6097              ; frame off. LaserFireHeld is cleared: the keys set it again each loop while fire is held.
 288+ 6097              LaserReady              equ 0
 289+ 6097              LaserOn                 equ 1
 290+ 6097              LaserOff                equ 2
 291+ 6097              LaserRest               equ 3
 292+ 6097              LaserMaxFrames          equ 8

 493+ 622B              ; The space station's safe zone (as BBC Elite): inside the cube |x|, |y|, |z| < $C000 round the planet (sign bytes no
 494+ 622B              ; integer bits, hi bytes < $C0). SpaceStationSafeZone is 0 inside, $FF outside (SetSafeZone / ClearSafeZone); the spawn
 495+ 622B              ; tables, the status screen and the station's arrival use it. On flying in, if slot 0 (kept for it) is free, the station
 496+ 622B              ; is made there: on the line from the planet's centre towards us, |normal| * 192 out (49000 at most, as BBC's 2 nosev

   2+ 6A27              ; The hyperspace countdown, timed by FrameCounter16 (the interrupt's 50 Hz count, which stops while paused) so a second is
   3+ 6A27              ; a second however fast the main loop runs. OuterHyperCount is the seconds left, shown 11 to 1; the jump starts when it

   5+ 6A27              ; HyperSpaceMessage (main loop, views) draws the text every loop and clears it once when the count stops.
   6+ 6A27

 189+ 7052              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 190+ 7052              ; DrawSunDistance / DrawPlanetDistance / DrawStationDistance: print the integer part of the distance to the sun, planet
 191+ 7052              ; and space station on layer 2 to the right of their compass sprites.
 192+ 7052              ; The compass sprites sit in the left border (sprite x 0-33, top y = Sun/Planet/StationCompassTLY, layer 2 is offset by
 193+ 7052              ; 32,32 from sprite coordinates), so the text goes at the left of the 3D view, centred on each compass where possible.
 194+ 7052              ; That area is cleared every frame, so these are called every frame from the main loop rather than from UpdateConsole,
 195+ 7052              ; which only runs on console refresh frames.
 196+ 7052              ; Distance ~= max + 3/8 (mid + min) of |x|, |y|, |z| (within about +13% / -3%), using the integer part of each
 197+ 7052              ; S15.8 position (sign byte bits 0-6 and the hi byte), so it fits 16 bits (max 57341)
 198+ 7052              DistanceCol             equ 4
 199+ 7052              SunDistanceRow          equ 2                                       ; sun compass centre is above layer 2, so top text row
 200+ 7052              PlanetDistanceRow       equ PlanetCompassTLY + 17 - 32 - 4          ; compass centre (top + 17) in layer 2 rows, less half a character
 201+ 7052              StationDistanceRow      equ StationCompassTLY + 17 - 32 - 4

 203+ 7052              PlanetDistanceColour    equ L2ColourGREEN_1

1255+ 78C6              ; Radar edge markers: when the sun, planet or space station is outside the scanner range in X or Z (|x| or |z| >= 64,
1256+ 78C6              ; the same limit the blips use, y is ignored) a dot is put on the scanner outline in its direction. The direction is the
1257+ 78C6              ; one a blip would use (column = x, row = z / 4) and the ray is stepped out a row at a time until it reaches the outline.
1258+ 78C6              ; The outline is not a true ellipse so its half widths are tabled, measured from the console image: columns 59-196,
1259+ 78C6              ; rows 155-190, centre 127.5, 172.5 (left and right are symmetric about it)

  56+ 9038              ; ">getRank, de = kill count, returns a = index,hl destroyed"
  57+ 9038              ; ">Note for ranking first 2 bytes are target rank"

  59+ 9039 B3               or      e

  62+ 903D AF               xor     a

  67+ 9043 46               ld      b,(hl)                          ; bc = ranking

  76+ 904E 23               inc     hl
  77+ 904F 3C               inc     a                               ; we canloop forever as if kills was $FFFF then hits nutter rank but also +1 = 0000 as its 16 bit
  78+ 9050 18 EF            jr      .testLoop

  32+ 9D78 EB                               ex      de,hl       ; de = de + rs
  33+ 9D79              .LL126:             ShiftHLRight1
  33+ 9D79 CB 3C       >               srl h
  33+ 9D7B CB 1D       >               rr  l
  34+ 9D7D CB 20                            sla b
  35+ 9D7F 38 F5                            jr      c,.LL125
  36+ 9D81 20 F6                            jr      nz,.LL126
  37+ 9D83 EB                               ex      de,hl   ; hl = result
  38+ 9D84 D1 C1                            pop     bc,,de
  39+ 9D86 C9                               ret
  40+ 9D87
  41+ 9D87              ; hl = de * hl where de & hl are small enough to always ne 16 bit result, replaces mulDEbyHL
  42+ 9D87 C5           HLequDEmulHL:       push    bc
  43+ 9D88 7A                               ld      a,d                     ; a = x1
  44+ 9D89 54                               ld      d,h                     ; d = y1
  45+ 9D8A 67                               ld      h,a                     ; h = x1
  46+ 9D8B 4B                               ld      c,e                     ; c = x0
  47+ 9D8C 45                               ld      b,l                     ; b = y0
  48+ 9D8D ED 30                            mul     de                      ; y1 * y0
  49+ 9D8F EB                               ex      de,hl
  50+ 9D90 ED 30                            mul     de                      ; x1 * y0
  51+ 9D92 19                               add     hl,de                   ; add cross products
  52+ 9D93 59                               ld      e,c
  53+ 9D94 50                               ld      d,b
  54+ 9D95 ED 30                            mul     de                      ; y0 * x0
  55+ 9D97 7D                               ld      a,l                     ; cross products lsb
  56+ 9D98 82                               add     a,d                     ; add to msb final
  57+ 9D99 67                               ld      h,a
  58+ 9D9A 6B                               ld      l,e                     ; hl = final
  59+ 9D9B                                  ; 83 cycles, 19 bytes
  60+ 9D9B AF                               xor     a                       ; reset carry
  61+ 9D9C C1                               pop     bc
  62+ 9D9D C9                               ret
  63+ 9D9E              HLequHLmulDEu:
  64+ 9D9E              ;H.L = H.L * D.E unsigned 8.8 (bits 8-23 of the 32 bit product, so truncated), no sign handling
  65+ 9D9E CD A4 9D                         call    fixedS78_mulu       ; DE.HL = product
  66+ 9DA1 6C                               ld      l,h                 ; l = bits 8-15
  67+ 9DA2 63                               ld      h,e                 ; h = bits 16-23
  68+ 9DA3 C9                               ret
  69+ 9DA4              ;DE.HL = D.E * H.L as  7.8 Fixed Point unsigned maths, when doing 24 bit maths scale down to 8.8 as its accurate enough
  70+ 9DA4              fixedS78_mulu:      ;
  71+ 9DA4 7A           .checkZeroMul:      ld      a,d
  72+ 9DA5 B3                               or      e
  73+ 9DA6 CA CE 9D                         jp      z,.resultIsZero
  74+ 9DA9 7C                               ld      a,h
  75+ 9DAA B5                               or      l
  76+ 9DAB CA CE 9D                         jp      z, .resultIsZero
  77+ 9DAE 45           .performMultiplyU:  ld      b,l                 ; b = x0
  78+ 9DAF 4B                               ld      c,e                 ; c =  y0
  79+ 9DB0 5D                               ld      e,l                 ; e = x0
  80+ 9DB1 6A                               ld      l,d                 ; l = y1 d is already y1
  81+ 9DB2 E5                               push    hl                  ; save x1 y1 to stack
  82+ 9DB3 69                               ld      l,c                 ; l = y0
  83+ 9DB4 ED 30                            mul     de                  ; hl  = y1 * x0
  84+ 9DB6 EB                               ex      de,hl               ; . also setting de to x1 y0 as we prepped them in advance
  85+ 9DB7 ED 30                            mul     de                  ; x1*y0
  86+ 9DB9                                  ZeroA
  86+ 9DB9 AF          >                        xor a
  87+ 9DBA 19                               add     hl,de               ; sum cross products of y1*x0, x1 * y0 as they require no shifting
  88+ 9DBB 8F                               adc     a,a                 ; and capture carry bit ready for p3
  89+ 9DBC 59                               ld      e,c                 ; de = x0 * y0
  90+ 9DBD 50                               ld      d,b                 ; .
  91+ 9DBE ED 30                            mul     de                  ; .
  92+ 9DC0 47                               ld      b,a                 ; carry from cross products setting bc to <c>h  (where <c> is carry flag)
  93+ 9DC1 4C                               ld      c,h                 ; .
  94+ 9DC2 7A                               ld      a,d                 ; h = high byte of x0 * y 0 _ lower byte of cross product of y1 * x0
  95+ 9DC3 85                               add     a,l                 ; .
  96+ 9DC4 67                               ld      h,a                 ; .)
  97+ 9DC5 6B                               ld      l,e                 ; so now we have lower btwo bytes of result in HL (p1 p0)
  98+ 9DC6 D1                               pop de                      ; get x1 and y1 back from stack into de ready for multiply
  99+ 9DC7 ED 30                            mul de                      ; hl = x1*y1 and de = p1 p0
 100+ 9DC9 EB                               ex de,hl                    ; .
 101+ 9DCA ED 4A                            adc hl,bc                   ; hl = (x1 * y1) + <c>h (where h is upper byte of cross product from above)
 102+ 9DCC EB                               ex de,hl                    ; swap over de and hl for final result
 103+ 9DCD C9                               ret
 104+ 9DCE 11 00 00     .resultIsZero:      ld      de,0
 105+ 9DD1 21 00 00                         ld      hl,0
 106+ 9DD4 C9                               ret
 107+ 9DD5

 535  9E0F                  INCLUDE "./Maths/asm_arctan.asm"
# file opened: asm_arctan.asm
   1+ 9E0F              ;Calculate A = arctan(P / Q)
   2+ 9E0F              ; This finds the angle in the right-angled triangle where the opposite side to angle A is length P and the adjacent side to angle A has
   3+ 9E0F              ; length Q, so:  tan(A) = P / Q
   4+ 9E0F              ;
   5+ 9E0F              ; The result in A is an integer representing the angle in radians. The routine returns values in the range 0 to 128,  (or 0 to PI radians).
   6+ 9E0F 3A 7E 84     ARCTAN:                 ld      a,(varP)                    ; LDA P                  \ Set T1 = P EOR Q, which will have the sign of P * Q
   7+ 9E12 21 B0 85                             ld      hl,varQ                     ; EOR Q
   8+ 9E15 AE                                   xor     (hl)                        ; .
   9+ 9E16 32 7B 84                             ld      (varT1),a                   ; STA T1
  10+ 9E19 3A B0 85                             ld      a,(varQ)                    ; LDA Q                  \ If Q = 0, jump to AR2 to return a right angle
  11+ 9E1C A7                                   and     a                           ; BEQ AR2
  12+ 9E1D CA 5F 9E                             jp      z, .AR2                     ; .
  13+ 9E20 CB 27                                sla     a                           ; ASL A                  \ Set Q = |Q| * 2 (this is a quick way of clearing the
  14+ 9E22 32 B0 85                             ld      (varQ),a                    ; STA Q                  \ sign bit, and we don't need to shift right again as we only ever use this value in the division with |P| * 2, which we set next)
  15+ 9E25 3A 7E 84                             ld      a,(varP)                    ; LDA P                  \ Set A = |P| * 2
  16+ 9E28 CB 27                                sla     a                           ; ASL A
  17+ 9E2A 32 7E 84                             ld      (varP),a
  18+ 9E2D 21 B0 85                             ld      hl,varQ
  19+ 9E30 BE                                   cp      (hl)                        ; CMP Q                  \ If A >= Q, i.e. |P| > |Q|, jump to AR1 to swap P
  20+ 9E31 D2 43 9E                             jp      nc, .AR1                    ; BCS AR1                \ and Q around, so we can still use the lookup table
  21+ 9E34 CD 6B 9E                             call    ARS1                        ; JSR ARS1               \ Call ARS1 to set the following from the lookup table:  A = arctan(A / Q)  = arctan(|P / Q|)
  22+ 9E37                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag so the SBC instruction in AR3 will be correct, should we jump there
  22+ 9E37 B7          >                        or a
  23+ 9E38 4F           .AR4:                   ld      c,a                         ; as we have to use a we use c as a temp, we can't push af as we would loose flags on pop
  24+ 9E39 3A 7B 84                             ld      a,(varT1)                   ; LDX T1                 \ If T1 is negative, i.e. P and Q have different signs,
  25+ 9E3C 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; .
  26+ 9E3D A7                                   and     a                           ; BMI AR3                \ jump down to AR3 to return arctan(-|P / Q|)
  27+ 9E3E 79                                   ld      a,c                         ; .                      \ we need to get a back before jump
  28+ 9E3F FA 62 9E                             jp      m, .AR3                     ; .
  29+ 9E42 C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Otherwise P and Q have the same sign, so our result is correct and we can return from the subroutine
  30+ 9E43              ; We want to calculate arctan(t) where |t| > 1, so we can use the calculation described in the documentation for the ACT table, i.e. 64 - arctan(1 / t)
  31+ 9E43              ; In the 6502 verion it works with A already being P but we will fetch it
  32+ 9E43 3A B0 85     .AR1:                   ld      a,(varQ)                    ; LDX Q                  \ Swap the values in Q and P, using the fact that we
  33+ 9E46 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; .
  34+ 9E47 3A 7E 84                             ld      a,(varP)                    ; STA Q                  \ called AR1 with A = P
  35+ 9E4A 32 B0 85                             ld      (varQ),a                    ; .
  36+ 9E4D 78                                   ld      a,b                         ; TXA                    \ This also sets A = P (which now contains the original argument |Q|)
  37+ 9E4E 32 7E 84                             ld      (varP),a                    ; STX P                  \
  38+ 9E51 CD 6B 9E                             call    ARS1                        ; JSR ARS1               \ Call ARS1 to set the following from the lookup table: A = arctan(A / Q) = arctan(|Q / P|) = arctan(1 / |P / Q|)
  39+ 9E54 32 CC 85                             ld      (varT),a                    ; STA T                  \ Set T = 64 - T, we use B as T (its not really that)
  40+ 9E57 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; its actually t = a, a = 64-a
  41+ 9E58 3E 40                                ld      a,64                        ; LDA #64 What is going on here is t = result
  42+ 9E5A                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SBC T                            a = 64- result
  42+ 9E5A B7          >                        or a
  43+ 9E5B 98                                   sbc     a,b                         ; .
  44+ 9E5C C3 38 9E                             jp      .AR4                        ; BCS AR4                \ Jump to AR4 to continue the calculation (this BCS is effectively a JMP as the subtraction will never underflow, as ARS1 returns values in the range 0-31)
  45+ 9E5F              ; If we get here then Q = 0, so tan(A) = infinity and A is a right angle, or 0.25 of a circle. We allocate 255 to a full circle, so we should return 63 for a right angle
  46+ 9E5F 3E 3F        .AR2:                   ld      a,63                        ; LDA #63                \ Set A to 63, to represent a right angle
  47+ 9E61 C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  48+ 9E62              ; A contains arctan(|P / Q|) but P and Q have different signs, so we need to return arctan(-|P / Q|), using the calculation described in the documentation for the ACT table, i.e. 128 - A
  49+ 9E62 32 CC 85     .AR3:                   ld      (varT),a
  50+ 9E65 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; STA T                  \ Set A = 128 - A, we use b as T
  51+ 9E66 3E 80                                ld      a,128                       ; LDA #128               \
  52+ 9E68                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SBC T                  \ The subtraction will work because we did a SEC before calling AR3
  52+ 9E68 B7          >                        or a
  53+ 9E69 98                                   sbc     a,b
  54+ 9E6A C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  55+ 9E6B              ; This routine fetches arctan(A / Q) from the ACT table, so A will be set to an integer in the range 0 to 31 that represents an angle from 0 to 45 degrees (or 0 to \ PI / 4 radians)
  56+ 9E6B              ARS1:                   MMUSelectMathsTables
  56+ 9E6B ED 91 50 63 >                     nextreg MathsTablesMMU,    BankMathsTables
  57+ 9E6F CD 9F 07                             call    Amul256DivQ                 ; JSR LL28               \ Call LL28 to calculate: R = 256 * A / Q
  58+ 9E72 3A B1 85                             ld      a,(varR)                    ; LDA R                  \ Set X = R / 8
  59+ 9E75 CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \       = 32 * A / Q
  60+ 9E77 CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \
  61+ 9E79 CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \ so X has the value t * 32 where t = A / Q, which is
  62+ 9E7B 21 A2 9E                             ld      hl,ACT                      ; TAX                    \ what we need to look up values in the ACT table
  63+ 9E7E ED 31                                add     hl,a                        ; LDA ACT,X              \ Fetch ACT+X from the ACT table into A, so now:
  64+ 9E80 7E                                   ld      a,(hl)                      ;                        \   A = value in ACT + X = value in ACT + (32 * A / Q)= arctan(A / Q)
  65+ 9E81 C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  66+ 9E82
  67+ 9E82
# file closed: asm_arctan.asm

   1+ 9FAA              ; A = A / D * 96 unsigned (A < D, else 96), the 6502 TIS2 shift and subtract. The remainder is 9 bit after each shift:
   2+ 9FAA              ; when the shift carries out it is over 255 so over D and must be subtracted (that carry was once dropped, so with D
   3+ 9FAA              ; over 128 the answer could be anything, e.g. 67 / 137 gave 1 not 46)
   4+ 9FAA              AequAdivQmul96ABS:      JumpIfAGTENusng d, .TIS2AccGTEQ			; if A >= Q then return with a 1 (unity i.e. 96) with the correct sign
   4+ 9FAA BA          >                        cp     d
   4+ 9FAB D2 C8 9F    >                        jp		nc,.TIS2AccGTEQ
   5+ 9FAE 06 FE                                ld			b,$FE						; division roll (replaced varT)
   6+ 9FB0 CB 27        .TIS2RollTLoop:			sla			a
   7+ 9FB2 38 04                                jr          c,.TIS2Sub                  ; 9 bit remainder >= 256 > d
   8+ 9FB4                                      JumpIfALTNusng d,.TIS2SkipSub           ; a < d so don;t subtract
   8+ 9FB4 BA          >                        cp      d
   8+ 9FB5 DA CB 9F    >                        jp		c, .TIS2SkipSub
   9+ 9FB8 92           .TIS2Sub:               sub			d							; remainder - d (mod 256 is right for the 9 bit case)
  10+ 9FB9 37                                   scf
  11+ 9FBA CB 10                                rl			b							; T rolled left to push bit out the end
  12+ 9FBC 38 F2                                jr			c,.TIS2RollTLoop				; if we still have not hit the empty marker continue
  13+ 9FBE 78           .TIS2SKIPCont:	        ld			a,b							; T
  14+ 9FBF CB 3F                                srl			a							; result / 2
  15+ 9FC1 CB 3F                                srl			a							; result / 4
  16+ 9FC3 47                                   ld			b,a							; t = t /4
  17+ 9FC4 CB 3F                                srl			a							; result / 8
  18+ 9FC6 80                                   add			a,b							; result /8 + result /4
  19+ 9FC7 C9                                   ret

  25+ 9FD0 C3 BE 9F                             jp			.TIS2SKIPCont

  40+ 9FDC C8                                   ret         z       ; (was sla a / ret z which also exited with 0 for d = 128)

 546  A093                  INCLUDE "./Maths/Utilities/badd_ll38.asm"
# file opened: badd_ll38.asm
   1+ A093              baddll38:				;.LL38	\ -> &4812 \ BADD(S)A=R+Q(SA) \ byte add (subtract)   (Sign S)A = R + Q*(Sign from A^S)
   2+ A093              SAEquSRPlusAQ:
   3+ A093              ; Calculate the following between sign-magnitude numbers:
   4+ A093              ;   (S A) = (S R) + (A Q)
   5+ A093              ; where the sign bytes only contain the sign bits, not magnitudes.
   6+ A093              ; note goes wrong at <-127 >128 so need 16 bit version
   7+ A093              ; so need to fix the issue with carry flag not returning a fault correctly
   8+ A093              LL38:
   9+ A093              ; calculation table
  10+ A093              ;   R     Q    Op            Sign calc
  11+ A093              ;	10    5    Add           +    sign same add R sign
  12+ A093              ;   -10   5    ABS Sub       -    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  13+ A093              ;   10   -5    ABS sub       +    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  14+ A093              ;	-10  -5    ABS Add       -    sign same add R sign
  15+ A093              ;   5    10    Add           +    sign same add R sign
  16+ A093              ;   -5   10    Swap ABS SUB  +    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB Q sign
  17+ A093              ;   5    -10   swap ABS Sub  -    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB R sign
  18+ A093              ;   -5   -10   ABS  add      -    sign same add R sign
  19+ A093
  20+ A093              ;   -10   5    ABS Sub       -    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  21+ A093              ;   10   -5    ABS sub       +    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  22+ A093              ;   -5   10    Swap ABS SUB  +    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB Q sign
  23+ A093              ;   5    -10   swap ABS Sub  -    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB R sign
  24+ A093
  25+ A093
  26+ A093              ; Calculate sign for Q from A and varS
  27+ A093 21 B2 85     	ld		hl,varS							;
  28+ A096 AE           	xor		(hl)							;  EOR &83		\ S	\ sign of operator is A xor S
  29+ A097 FA A2 A0     	jp		m,.LL39Subtraction  			; if signs are different then we have subtraction
  30+ A09A 3A B0 85     	ld		a,(varQ)						; Q	\ else addition, S already correct
  31+ A09D 21 B1 85     	ld		hl,varR
  32+ A0A0 86           	add		a,(hl)							; a = Q + R
  33+ A0A1 C9           	ret										; Done carry set if overflow
  34+ A0A2              .LL39Subtraction:							; 1 byte subtraction (S)A = R-Q
  35+ A0A2 3A B1 85     	ld		a,(varR)						; a = R
  36+ A0A5 21 B0 85     	ld		hl,varQ                         ; Q
  37+ A0A8              ;--	JumpIfALTMemHLusng LL39SwapSubtraction	; if a < (hl) then do LL39SwapSubtraction
  38+ A0A8              	ClearCarryFlag                          ; we need to not use carry (6502 is different that it uses the compliement)
  38+ A0A8 B7          >                        or a
  39+ A0A9 9E           	sbc		a,(hl)							; A = R - Q which as R >= Q will always be a positive result
  40+ A0AA 38 01            jr      c,.LL39SignCorrection
  41+ A0AC              ;--    jr      a,.LL39ResultZero
  42+ A0AC              ;--   JumpIfNegative LL39SignCorrection		; if there was underflow we have to correct sign
  43+ A0AC              ;--	or		a								; Clear carry flag to say result is correct
  44+ A0AC C9           	ret
  45+ A0AD              .LL39SignCorrection:

 128+ A219              ; Missile blast (splash damage). Call with the exploding missile's bank paged in (it must already be flagged exploding so it

 130+ A219              ; The range is a fraction in 1/256ths (S15.8 lo byte, so 0.0 to 0.996), e.g. 51 = 0.2. Space stations are immune.
 131+ A219              ; MissileDirectHitSlot (slot, MissileHitPlayer or MissileNoDirectHit) is skipped as a direct hit has already been damaged

 181++A513              ; AHL = BHL + CDE in S15.8 lead sign, saturating. AHLequBHLplusCDE does not detect overflow: with the same signs a magnitude
 182++A513              ; sum >= 32768.0 carries into bit 7 and flips the sign, which would point the missile the wrong way. Opposite signs can not
 183++A513              ; overflow. On overflow the result is clamped to B's sign with the maximum magnitude (direction is all that matters then).
 184++A513              ; Needs the maths banked fns paged in. Destroys C and DE, preserves B
 185++A513 78           MissileVectorAdd:       ld      a,b
 186++A514 A9                                   xor     c
 187++A515 FA 00 00                             jp      m,AHLequBHLplusCDE                  ; opposite signs, can not overflow, implicit ret
 188++A518 CD 00 00                             call    AHLequBHLplusCDE
 189++A51B 4F                                   ld      c,a                                 ; did the sign change
 190++A51C A8                                   xor     b                                   ; .
 191++A51D 79                                   ld      a,c                                 ; .
 192++A51E F0                                   ret     p                                   ; no so no overflow
 193++A51F 78                                   ld      a,b                                 ; overflow so saturate

   1+ C6C3              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2+ C6C3              ; The system map (the extended keyboard's EDIT key, in flight): a flat top down map of the local system round us, x across
   3+ C6C3              ; and z up the screen (ahead is up, as we always look along z), y (height) left out of the plot and shown as a + / - number
   4+ C6C3              ; of units beside each body. The sun, the planet and the space station are marked and named, other ships are dots (red if
   5+ C6C3              ; hostile). The scale is a power of 2 chosen so the sun, planet and station all fit; ships further out are left off.
   6+ C6C3              ; Positions come from SystemMapGather (main memory, as the sun, planet and ship banks page into slot 6, where this code
   7+ C6C3              ; is). It is redrawn twice a second (loop_system_map), erasing only what it drew the time before, so it doesn't flicker.
   8+ C6C3              ; In BankMenuSystem with the system data screen.
   9+ C6C3              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  10+ C6C3              SMapCentreX             equ 160                     ; us
  11+ C6C3              SMapCentreY             equ 134
  12+ C6C3              SMapRadius              equ 104                     ; the furthest a mark is drawn from us on either axis
  13+ C6C3              SMapRefreshFrames       equ FramesPerSecond / 2
  14+ C6C3              SMapLabelRight          equ 180                     ; a body's label goes on its right unless its column is this or more
  15+ C6C3              SMapPrevSize            equ 8                       ; per mark drawn: in use, row, column (2), label row, label column (2), label length
  16+ C6C3              SMapAxisColour          equ L2ColourGREY_4
  17+ C6C3              SMapTextRow             equ 244

 100+ E5B5              ; "l2_draw_horz_line_320"
 101+ E5B5              ; ">b = row; hl = col, de = length in pixels (1 = 1 pixel), c = color"
 102+ E5B5              ; ">clipped at the right edge (column 319); destroys a, bc, de, hl"
 103+ E5B5 7A           l2_draw_horz_line_320:  ld		a,d
 104+ E5B6 B3                                   or      e
 105+ E5B7 C8           .zerolengthexit:        ret		z
 106+ E5B8 C5 E5        .clipRight:             push    bc,,hl                      ; save row, colour and column
 107+ E5BA 19                                   add     hl,de                       ; hl = column after the last pixel
 108+ E5BB 01 40 01                             ld      bc,320                      ; past the right edge?
 109+ E5BE                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; .
 109+ E5BE B7          >                        or a
 110+ E5BF ED 42                                sbc     hl,bc                       ; hl = pixels past the edge
 111+ E5C1 38 09                                jr      c,.noClip                   ; none
 112+ E5C3 EB                                   ex      de,hl                       ; length -= pixels past the edge
 113+ E5C4                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; .
 113+ E5C4 B7          >                        or a
 114+ E5C5 ED 52                                sbc     hl,de                       ; .
 115+ E5C7 EB                                   ex      de,hl                       ; .
 116+ E5C8 38 24                                jr      c,.offScreen                ; started at or past column 320
 117+ E5CA 28 22                                jr      z,.offScreen                ; .

 119+ E5CE E5 C5        .longenoughtfordma:     push    hl,,bc                      ; (hl stays on the stack until done)
 120+ E5D0 CD C6 E0                             call    asm_l2_320_col_bank_select  ; Select the first bank to start writing to and adjust hl
 121+ E5D3 C1           .bankSelected:          pop     bc                          ; get back row and colour
 122+ E5D4 68                                   ld      l,b                         ; set target row
 123+ E5D5 71           .fillBank:              ld      (hl),c                      ; plot pixel
 124+ E5D6 1B                                   dec     de                          ; one less still to do
 125+ E5D7 7A                                   ld      a,d                         ; if we run out of DE then done
 126+ E5D8 B3                                   or      e                           ; .
 127+ E5D9 CA EC E5                             jp      z,.fillComplete             ; .
 128+ E5DC 24                                   inc     h                           ; move on one column
 129+ E5DD 7C                                   ld      a,h                         ; if we are done next bank
 130+ E5DE FE 40                                cp      64                          ; .
 131+ E5E0 C2 D5 E5                             jp      nz,.fillBank                ; else carry on
 132+ E5E3 C5           .nextBank:              push    bc
 133+ E5E4 CD 75 E1                             call    asm_l2_320_next_bank        ; cycle on one bank as we always go left to right
 134+ E5E7 26 00                                ld      h,0                         ; reset banked memory address colum to 0
 135+ E5E9 C3 D3 E5                             jp      .bankSelected
 136+ E5EC E1           .fillComplete:          pop     hl                          ; clean up stack on completion

 139+ E5F0 C9                                   ret

  62+ EC2C              ; l2_draw_6502_line - clip and draw a line in the Layer 2 upper two thirds (256x128, rows 0-63 bank 0, rows 64-127 bank 1)
  63+ EC2C              ; In : x1,y1,x2,y2 16 bit signed, nominally -1024..+1024 (any value within +/-2047 is safe)
  64+ EC2C              ;      colour from line_gfx_colour, Layer 2 code bank paged in (MMUSelectLayer2)
  65+ EC2C              ; Out: carry set   - line wholly outside the window, nothing drawn
  66+ EC2C              ;      carry clear - line drawn, x1,y1,x2,y2 hold the clipped end points (high bytes 0)
  67+ EC2C              ;      AF, BC, DE, HL, AF' destroyed, IX and IY preserved
  68+ EC2C              ; y1 = y2           horizontal, clamped without any maths, P1 = P2 plots a single pixel, long spans are a DMA fill
  69+ EC2C              ; x1 = x2           vertical, clamped without any maths, column fill split at the bank 0/1 boundary
  70+ EC2C              ; otherwise         Cohen-Sutherland outcodes for trivial accept/reject, edge intersections via 12x12 multiply and
  71+ EC2C              ;                   24/16 divide (rounded), then the clipped line is re-checked for pixel/horz/vert before an 8 bit Bresenham
  72+ EC2C              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  73+ EC2C              L2L_OC_LEFT_BIT         equ     0
  74+ EC2C              L2L_OC_RIGHT_BIT        equ     1
  75+ EC2C              L2L_OC_TOP_BIT          equ     2
  76+ EC2C              L2L_OC_BOTTOM_BIT       equ     3
  77+ EC2C              L2L_OC_LEFT             equ     1 << L2L_OC_LEFT_BIT            ; x < 0
  78+ EC2C              L2L_OC_RIGHT            equ     1 << L2L_OC_RIGHT_BIT           ; x > 255
  79+ EC2C              L2L_OC_TOP              equ     1 << L2L_OC_TOP_BIT             ; y < 0
  80+ EC2C              L2L_OC_BOTTOM           equ     1 << L2L_OC_BOTTOM_BIT          ; y > 127
  81+ EC2C              L2L_CLIP_MAX_X          equ     255
  82+ EC2C              L2L_CLIP_MAX_Y          equ     127

  84+ EC2C              L2L_DMA_MIN             equ     20                              ; spans this long or longer use DMA, the program upload costs ~20 pixels of CPU loop
  85+ EC2C              L2L_OPCODE_INC_L        equ     $2C
  86+ EC2C              L2L_OPCODE_DEC_L        equ     $2D
  87+ EC2C              L2L_DMA_WR1_FIXED_TIMED equ     $64                             ; WR1 port A memory, fixed address, timing byte follows

  89+ EC2C              L2L_DMA_CYCLE_2T        equ     $02                             ; timing byte, 2 T state cycle length

   1+ F03A              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2+ F03A              ; l2_fill_convex_polygon: a convex polygon filled in the 256 x 128 view (256 x 192 Layer 2, rows 0 to 127), for solid ships
   3+ F03A              ; (SOLID_HULL, Documentation/SolidHulls.md). Assembled in every build so it can be tested on its own.
   4+ F03A              ;   in:  ix = points, b of them (3 to PolyMaxPoints): x lo, x hi, y lo, y hi each, 16 bit 2's complement (off screen is
   5+ F03A              ;        fine), a = colour
   6+ F03A              ;   out: nothing; uses every register
   7+ F03A              ; Each edge is walked row by row from its top to its bottom (rows clipped to the view first), with x exact:
   8+ F03A              ; x(y) = xa + sign(dx) * floor((y - ya) * |dx| / dy), stepped as q = |dx| / dy, r = |dx| mod dy per row (one divide an
   9+ F03A              ; edge, and a 32 / 16 divide to start an edge that begins above the view). Each row keeps its smallest and largest x
  10+ F03A              ; (16 bit, so a polygon partly off the side is right), then each row's span is clipped to columns 0 to 255 and drawn with
  11+ F03A              ; l2_draw_horz_line. Both ends of every span are drawn, so faces that share an edge meet with no gap. No winding needed.
  12+ F03A              ; A flat polygon (every point on one row) is that row from its smallest to its largest x.
  13+ F03A              ; Tools/test_lines.py test_fill_convex_polygon checks it pixel for pixel against the same rules in Python
  14+ F03A              PolyMaxPoints           equ 8
  15+ F03A              PolyViewRows            equ 128
  16+ F03A

   2+ F58F              ; Solid ships (SOLID_HULL, Documentation/SolidHulls.md): SolidHullDraw, from ProcessShip after CullV2 with the ship's
   3+ F58F              ; universe bank in slot 6 and this (the Layer 2) bank in slot 7.
   4+ F58F              ;   carry set: drawn solid. In order: the hull's faces (sorted), the phase 2 polygons (ports: engines, later entrances
   5+ F58F              ;   and view ports), with SOLID_OUTLINES lines over it (ALL every visible edge, DECORATION only the decoration edges),
   6+ F58F              ;   then the table's lone lines (nose sensor / gun port lines, unless ALL drew them); carry clear: the caller draws the
   7+ F58F              ;   wireframe
   8+ F58F              ; Drawn solid when the model has a face table (Tools/ship_faces.py: ShipSolidFlag $00, copied to UBnkHullSolid), no vertex
   9+ F58F              ; is at or behind the camera (its z from ProcessNodes, in UBnkNodeArray2), and with WIREFRAME_FALLBACK its z is not less
  10+ F58F              ; than WIREFRAME_DISTANCE (eliteNext.asm). The table's polygons are the faces plus any fins (a fin is seen when any face
  11+ F58F              ; its edges are on faces us). The visible ones are painted furthest first (painter's algorithm), each one's depth its
  12+ F58F              ; furthest vertex, so on a hull that isn't convex a nearer face covers a further one. Colours, for now: a batch of 4 per
  13+ F58F              ; ship (by model id), alternating through the faces so each can be seen

 731  F855                  INCLUDE "./Layer2Graphics/l2_draw_line_v2.asm"
# file opened: l2_draw_line_v2.asm
   1+ F855              ; ******************************************************************************
   2+ F855              ;
   3+ F855              ;	Draw a pixel line from (x0,y0) defined in (COORDS) - the current plot
   4+ F855              ;	coordinate, to the relative distance points (x0+x,y0+y).
   5+ F855              ;
   6+ F855              ;	Design & programming by Gunther Strube,	Copyright (C) InterLogic 1995
   7+ F855              ;
   8+ F855              ;	The (COORDS+0)	pointer contains the current y coordinate, (COORDS+1) the
   9+ F855              ;	current x coordinate. The main program should reset the (COORDS) variables
  10+ F855              ;	before using line drawing.
  11+ F855              ;
  12+ F855              ;	The routine checks the range of specified coordinates which is the
  13+ F855              ;	boundaries of the graphics area (256x64	pixels).
  14+ F855              ;	If a boundary error occurs the routine exits automatically.	This may be
  15+ F855              ;	useful if you are trying to draw a line longer than allowed. Only the
  16+ F855              ;	visible part will be drawn.
  17+ F855              ;
  18+ F855              ;	The hardware graphics memory is organized as (0,0) in the top left corner.
  19+ F855              ;
  20+ F855              ;	The plot routine is	defined by an address pointer	in IX.
  21+ F855              ;
  22+ F855              ;	IN:	HL =	move	relative x horisontal points (maximum +/- 255).
  23+ F855              ;		DE =	move	relative y vertical	points (maximum +/-	255).
  24+ F855              ;		IX =	pointer to plot routine that uses HL = (x,y)	of plot coordinate.
  25+ F855              ;
  26+ F855              ;	OUT:	None.
  27+ F855              ;
  28+ F855              ;	Registers	used	by routine:
  29+ F855              ;		   N	:	B, loop counter
  30+ F855              ;		   i	:	line	balance variable
  31+ F855              ;		   x	:	H/L,	horisontal, vertical distance	variables
  32+ F855              ;		   y	:	H/L,	horisontal, vertical distance	variables
  33+ F855              ;	  (x0,y0)	:	(h,l)
  34+ F855              ;	  direc_x	:	d, horisontal step increment
  35+ F855              ;	  direc_y	:	e, vertical step increment
  36+ F855              ;		 ddx	:	b, horisontal step increment
  37+ F855              ;		 ddy	:	c, vertical step increment
  38+ F855              ;
  39+ F855              ;		DE, A work registers.
  40+ F855              ;
  41+ F855              ; The algorithm in pseudo-code:
  42+ F855              ;
  43+ F855              ;	direc_x =	SGN x: direc_y	= SGN y
  44+ F855              ;	x = ABS x: y =	ABS y
  45+ F855              ;
  46+ F855              ;	if x	>= y
  47+ F855              ;		if x+y=0 then return
  48+ F855              ;		H = x
  49+ F855              ;		L = y
  50+ F855              ;		ddx = direc_x
  51+ F855              ;		ddy = 0
  52+ F855              ;	else
  53+ F855              ;		H = y
  54+ F855              ;		L = x
  55+ F855              ;		ddx = 0
  56+ F855              ;		ddy = direc_y
  57+ F855              ;	endif
  58+ F855              ;
  59+ F855              ;	B = H
  60+ F855              ;	i = INT(B/2)
  61+ F855              ;	FOR N=B TO 1 STEP -1
  62+ F855              ;		i = i + L
  63+ F855              ;		if i	< H
  64+ F855              ;			ix =	ddx
  65+ F855              ;			iy =	ddy
  66+ F855              ;		else
  67+ F855              ;			i = i - H
  68+ F855              ;			ix =	direc_x
  69+ F855              ;			iy =	direc_y
  70+ F855              ;		endif
  71+ F855              ;		x0 =	x0 +	ix
  72+ F855              ;		y0 =	y0 +	iy
  73+ F855              ;		plot	(x0,y0)
  74+ F855              ;	NEXT	N
  75+ F855              ;
  76+ F855              ;
  77+ F855              ;	Registers	changed after return:
  78+ F855              ;		..BCDEHL/IXIY/af......	same
  79+ F855              ;		AF....../..../..bcdehl	different
  80+ F855              ;
  81+ F855 00 00        line_gfx_coords         dw  0
  82+ F857
  83+ F857              LineHLtoDE:
  84+ F857 7C           TestMaxY:               ld	a,h ; were h = y or l = y?
  85+ F858 FE C0                                cp	192
  86+ F85A 30 26                                jr	nc, exit_line		; y0	coordinate out	of range
  87+ F85C 7A                                   ld	a,d
  88+ F85D FE C0                                cp	192
  89+ F85F 30 21                                jr	nc, exit_line		; y1	coordinate out	of range
  90+ F861 22 55 F8                             ld	(line_gfx_coords),hl		; the starting	point is now default
  91+ F864 E5                                   push	hl
  92+ F865 D5                                   push	de
  93+ F866 6C                                   ld	l,h				; L = x0
  94+ F867 62                                   ld	h,d				; H = x1
  95+ F868 7C           distanceX:		        ld	a,h
  96+ F869 95                                   sub	l
  97+ F86A 6F                                   ld	l,a
  98+ F86B 26 00                                ld	h,0
  99+ F86D 30 02                                jr	nc, distanceXDone
 100+ F86F 26 FF                                ld	h,-1
 101+ F871 D1           distanceXDone:          pop	de
 102+ F872 E3                                   ex	(sp),hl			; L = y0

 117+ F883              ;	IN:	HL =	move	relative x horisontal points (maximum +/- 255).
 118+ F883              ;		DE =	move	relative y vertical	points (maximum +/-	255).
 119+ F883              ;
 120+ F883              ; OUT: h - l distance in	HL

 778  E00F              GetShipBank2Id:         MGetShipBankId ShipBankTable2
 778  E00F 06 00       >                        ld      b,0
 778  E011 4F          >                        ld      c,a                                 ; c= original ship id
 778  E012 CB 3F       >.ShiftLoop:             srl     a
 778  E014 CB 3F       >                        srl     a
 778  E016 CB 3F       >                        srl     a
 778  E018 CB 3F       >                        srl     a                                   ; divide by 16
 778  E01A 47          >                        ld      b,a                                 ; b = bank nbr
 778  E01B 79          >                        ld      a,c
 778  E01C 50          >                        ld      d,b
 778  E01D 1E 10       >                        ld      e,16
 778  E01F ED 30       >                        mul                                         ; de = 16 * bank number (max is about 15 banks)
 778  E021 93          >                        sub     e                                   ; a= actual model id now
 778  E022 50          >.SelectedBank:          ld      d,b                                 ; save current bank number
 778  E023 47          >                        ld      b,a                                 ; b = adjusted ship nbr
 778  E024 7A          >                        ld      a,d                                 ; a = bank number
 778  E025             >;.. Now b = bank and a = adjusted ship nbr
 778  E025 21 78 E0    >                        ld      hl,ShipBankTable2                        ; a= bank index
 778  E028 ED 31       >                        add     hl,a
 778  E02A ED 31       >                        add     hl,a
 778  E02C 7E          >                        ld      a,(hl)                              ; a = actual bank now
 778  E02D             >                        ClearCarryFlag
 778  E02D B7          >                        or a
 778  E02E C9          >                        ret

 210+ E0BC              ;    Spr,   pattern     spr+1, pattern+1

 212+ E0BC              ; " sprite_big BC = row, hl= col D = sprite nbr , E= , pattern"
 213+ E0BC              ; note, BC and HL must be in correct range else they will mess up other byte's attributes, not masked for speed

 215+ E0BC              ; Currently can not get realtive sprites to work so will brute force it.

 217+ E0BD F6 C0                                    or      %11000000                                                   ; Enable visible and 5th byte

   1+ C000              ;    DEFINE DEBUGMISSILELAUNCH 1
   2+ C000              ;    DEFINE PLOTPOINTSONLY 1
   3+ C000                ;DEFINE OVERLAYNODES 1
   4+ C000              ; In  flight ship data tables
   5+ C000              ; In  flight ship data tables
   6+ C000              ; There can be upto &12 objects in flight.
   7+ C000              ; To avoid hassle of memory heap managment, the free list
   8+ C000              ; will correspond to a memory bank offset so data will be held in
   9+ C000              ; 1 bank per universe object. Its a waste of a lot of memory but really
  10+ C000              ; 1 bank per universe object. Its a waste of a lot of memory but really
  11+ C000              ; simple that way. Each bank will be 8K and swapped on 8K slot 7 $E000 to $FFFF
  12+ C000              ; This means each gets its own line list, inwork etc

 145++C0BE              ; UBnKSpawnObject - signals on death to spawn cargo items
 146++C0BE              ; 0 -                   Spawn Cargo 1
 147++C0BE              ; 1 -                   Spawn Cargo 2

 155++C0BE              ; UBnkaiatkecm
 156++C0BE              ; Bit	                Description
 157++C0BE              ; 7 -                   AI Enabled Flag
 158++C0BE              ; 6 -                   Ship Visible = ShipOnScreen/NotCloaked (cleared or set by check visible or cloaking override)
 159++C0BE              ; 5 -                   Ship is exploding if set, note if its a missile and one already equeued this will have to linger
 160++C0BE              ;                       linger can be done by not erasing ship unit missile equeue handled
 161++C0BE              ; 4 -                   Ship marked as exploded, cleared once aknowledged then bit 5 takes over and UBnKCloudCounter
 162++C0BE              ; 3 -                   Display state - Plot as a Dot
 163++C0BE              ; 2 -                   Nbr of Missiles bit 2
 164++C0BE              ; 1 -                   Nbr of Missiles bit 1
 165++C0BE              ; 0 -                   ECM present flag
 166++C0BE              ; ShipNewBitsAddr (in blueprint)
 167++C0BE              ;Bit	                Description
 168++C0BE              ;#0	Trader flag         * 0 = not a trader  * 1 = trader
 169++C0BE              ;                       80% of traders are peaceful and mind their own business plying their trade between the planet and space station, but 20% of them moonlight as bounty hunters (see bit #1)
 170++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are traders: Escape pod, Shuttle, Transporter, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Worm
 171++C0BE              ;#1 Bounty hunter flag  * 0 = not a bounty hunter* 1 = bounty hunter
 172++C0BE              ;                       If we are a fugitive or a serious offender and we bump into a bounty hunter, they will become hostile and attack us (see bit #2)
 173++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are bounty hunters: Viper, Fer-de-lance
 174++C0BE              ;#2	Hostile flag        * 0 = not hostile  * 1 = hostile
 175++C0BE              ;                       Hostile ships will attack us on sight; there are quite a few of them
 176++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are hostile: Sidewinder, Mamba, Krait, Adder, Gecko, Cobra Mk I, Worm, Cobra Mk III, Asp Mk II, Python (pirate), Moray, Thargoid, Thargon, Constrictor
 177++C0BE              ;#3	Pirate flag         * 0 = not a pirate * 1 = pirate
 178++C0BE              ;                       Hostile pirates will attack us on sight, but once we get inside the space station safe zone, they will stop
 179++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are pirates: Sidewinder, Mamba, Krait, Adder, Gecko, Cobra Mk I, Cobra Mk III, Asp Mk II, Python (pirate), Moray, Thargoid
 180++C0BE              ;#4	Docking flag        * 0 = not docking * 1 = docking
 181++C0BE              ;                       Traders with their docking flag set fly towards the space station to try to dock, otherwise they aim for the planet
 182++C0BE              ;                       This flag is randomly set for traders when they are spawned
 183++C0BE              ;                       Ships that can be docking: Escape pod, Shuttle, Transporter, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Worm
 184++C0BE              ;#5	Innocent bystander  * 0 = normal * 1 = innocent bystander
 185++C0BE              ;                       If we attack an innocent ship within the space station safe zone, then the station will get angry with us and start spawning cops
 186++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are innocent bystanders: Shuttle, Transporter, Cobra Mk III, Python, Boa, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Cougar
 187++C0BE              ;#6	Cop flag            * 0 = not a cop * 1 = cop
 188++C0BE              ;                       If we destroy a cop, then we instantly become a fugitive (the Transporter isn't actually a cop, but it's clearly under police protection)
 189++C0BE              ;                       Ships that are cops: Viper, Transporter
 190++C0BE              ;#7	Scooped, docked, escape pod flag
 191++C0BE              ;                       For spawned ships, this flag indicates that the ship been scooped or has docked (bit 7 is always clear on spawning)
 192++C0BE              ;                       For blueprints, this flag indicates whether the ship type has an escape pod fitted, so it can launch it when in dire straits
 193++C0BE              ;                       Ships that have escape pods: Cobra Mk III, Python, Boa, Anaconda, Rock hermit, Viper, Mamba, Krait, Adder, Cobra Mk I, Cobra Mk III (pirate), Asp Mk II, Python (pirate), Fer-de-lance

1323+ D738              ; Pitch and roll are 2 phases
1324+ D738              ; 1 - we apply our pitch and roll to the ship position
1325+ D738              ;       x -> x + alpha * (y - alpha * x)
1326+ D738              ;       y -> y - alpha * x - beta * z
1327+ D738              ;       z -> z + beta * (y - alpha * x - beta * z)
1328+ D738              ; which can be simplified as:
1329+ D738              ;       1. K2 = y - alpha * x
1330+ D738              ;       2. z = z + beta * K2
1331+ D738              ;       3. y = K2 - beta * z
1332+ D738              ;       4. x = x + alpha * y
1333+ D738              ; 2 - we apply our patch and roll to the ship orientation
1334+ D738              ;      Roll calculations:
1335+ D738              ;
1336+ D738              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - alpha * nosev_x_hi
1337+ D738              ;        nosev_x = nosev_x + alpha * nosev_y_hi
1338+ D738              ;      Pitch calculations:
1339+ D738              ;
1340+ D738              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - beta * nosev_z_hi
1341+ D738              ;        nosev_z = nosev_z + beta * nosev_y_hi
1342+ D738

 207+ C290              ; -------------------------------------------------------------
 208+ C290              ; Sun Position    z = ((seed.d & 7) | 1)      shift left 16
 209+ C290              ;                 x = (seed.f & 3) shift left 16  | seed.f & 3 << 8 * -1 if seed f odd
 210+ C290              ;                 y    = sun x position
 211+ C290              ;
 212+ C290              CalculateSunWarpPositon:
 213+ C290 3A 43 86     .CalcZPosition:         ld      a,(WorkingSeeds+3)      ; seed d & 7
 214+ C293 E6 07                                and     %00000111               ; .
 215+ C295 F6 81                                or      %10000001               ; | 1
 216+ C297 32 18 C0     .SetZPosition:          ld      (SBnKzsgn),a            ; << 16 (i.e. load into z sign byte
 217+ C29A 21 00 00                             ld      hl, $0000               ; now set z hi and lo
 218+ C29D 22 16 C0                             ld      (SBnKzlo),hl            ;
 219+ C2A0 3A 45 86     .CalcXandYPosition:     ld      a,(WorkingSeeds+5)      ; seed f & 3
 220+ C2A3 E6 03                                and     %00000011               ; .
 221+ C2A5 47                                   ld      b,a
 222+ C2A6 3A 44 86                             ld      a,(WorkingSeeds+4)      ; get low bit of seed e
 223+ C2A9 E6 01                                and     %00000001
 224+ C2AB 1F                                   rra                             ; roll bi t0 into bit 7
 225+ C2AC B0                                   or      b                       ; now calc is f & 3 * -1 if seed e is odd
 226+ C2AD 32 12 C0     .SetXandYPosition:      ld      (SBnKxsgn),a            ; set into x and y sign byte
 227+ C2B0 32 15 C0                             ld      (SBnKysgn),a            ; .
 228+ C2B3 78                                   ld      a,b                     ; we want just seed f & 3 here
 229+ C2B4 32 11 C0                             ld      (SBnKxhi),a             ; set into x and y high byte
 230+ C2B7 32 14 C0                             ld      (SBnKyhi),a             ; .
 231+ C2BA                                      ZeroA

 513+ C4C6
 514+ C4C6              ; Pitch and roll are 2 phases
 515+ C4C6              ; 1 - we apply our pitch and roll to the ship position
 516+ C4C6              ;       x -> x + alpha * (y - alpha * x)
 517+ C4C6              ;       y -> y - alpha * x - beta * z
 518+ C4C6              ;       z -> z + beta * (y - alpha * x - beta * z)
 519+ C4C6              ; which can be simplified as:
 520+ C4C6              ;       1. K2 = y - alpha * x
 521+ C4C6              ;       2. z = z + beta * K2
 522+ C4C6              ;       3. y = K2 - beta * z
 523+ C4C6              ;       4. x = x + alpha * y
 524+ C4C6              ; 2 - we apply our patch and roll to the ship orientation
 525+ C4C6              ;      Roll calculations:
 526+ C4C6              ;
 527+ C4C6              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - alpha * nosev_x_hi
 528+ C4C6              ;        nosev_x = nosev_x + alpha * nosev_y_hi
 529+ C4C6              ;      Pitch calculations:
 530+ C4C6              ;
 531+ C4C6              ;        nosev_y = nosev_y - beta * nosev_z_hi
 532+ C4C6              ;        nosev_z = nosev_z + beta * nosev_y_hi
 533+ C4C6
 534+ C4C6
 535+ C4C6                          INCLUDE "./Universe/Sun/SunApplyMyRollAndPitch.asm"

  22++C4C6              ; Sun version of pitch and roll is a 24 bit calculation 1 bit sign + 23 bit value
  23++C4C6              ; Need to write a test routine for roll and pitchs
  24++C4C6              ; Minsky Roll       Minsky Pitch
  25++C4C6              ;  y -= alpha * x    y -= beta * z
  26++C4C6              ;  x += alpha * y    z += beta * y
  27++C4C6              ; or once combined
  28++C4C6              ;   1. K2 = y - alpha * x
  29++C4C6              ;   2. z = z + beta * K2
  30++C4C6              ;   3. y = K2 - beta * z
  31++C4C6              ;   4. x = x + alpha * y
  32++C4C6              ;------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  33++C4C6              ;	alpha = flight_roll / 256.0;
  34++C4C6              ;	beta = flight_climb / 256.0;

  36++C4C6              ;	z = z + beta * k2;

 913+ C735              ;.. We can use the circle draw logic gtom Bressenham's algorithm
 914+ C735              ; so now there are the following conditions to consider
 915+ C735              ; y min = 0   y center is negative radius <= ABS (Y center)             => Don't draw
 916+ C735              ; y min = 0   y center is negative radius > ABS (Y center)+1            => Draw bottom half only
 917+ C735              ; y max = 127 y center is > 127    radius <= y center - 127             => Don't draw
 918+ C735              ; y max = 127 y center is > 127    radius > y center - 127              => Draw top half only
 919+ C735              ; y min >= 0  y center > y min     we don't need to worry about radius  => Draw both halves
 920+ C735              ; x center + radius < 0                                                 => Don't draw
 921+ C735              ; x center - radius > 255                                               => Don't draw
 922+ C735              ; we won't consider x more here as the driver is the y coordinate but we will check if x is vaiable
 923+ C735              ; x point = max (x point, 0)   on left

 538+ C3AB              ; .........................................................................................................................
 539+ C3AB              ; we only hit this if z is positive so we can ignore signs
 540+ C3AB              ; radius = 16384 / (z / 256): BBC Elite uses 24576 (on the same X / (Z / 256) scale as the projected centre), scaled to
 541+ C3AB              ; 2/3 as our view is 128 rows high against the BBC 192, so the size still grows in step with
 542+ C3AB              ; the position. Worked as 32768 / (z / 128) for an extra bit of precision: PlanetUpdateAndRender only draws when
 543+ C3AB              ; z sign < 48 and z >= 256, so z / 128 is 2..24575 and fits the 16 bit divisor. Any radius 1..248 (odd or even)
 544+ C3AB              ; so the planet grows a pixel at a time rather than jumping

 549+ C3B4 17                                   rla                                  ; . carry = z bit 7

 332+ E0F8 21 00 E0     init_keyboard:          ld		hl,Keys                         ; no key s are pressed by default

 340+ E104 DD 21 38 E0  scan_keyboard:          ld		ix,RawKeys                      ; hl = table of raw IO port readings
 341+ E108 21 42 E0                             ld		hl,KeyAddrTab                   ; de = table of IO ports to read
 342+ E10B 0E 08                                ld		c,8                             ; 8 ports to ready
 343+ E10D 11 00 E0                             ld      de,Keys                         ; ix = table of key states from raw read
 344+ E110 7E           .PortReadLoop:          ld		a,(hl)							; Set up port to read as (hl)$FE
 345+ E111 DB FE                                in		a,($FE)							; read port to a
 346+ E113 DD 77 00                             ld      (ix+0),a                        ; save raw scan
 347+ E116 DD 23                                inc     ix
 348+ E118 23                                   inc		hl                              ; and ready for next read
 349+ E119 06 05        .ProcessInputBits:      ld		b,5								; loop all bits (there are only 5 keys to a group)
 350+ E11B 1F           .ProcessBitsLoop:       rra                                     ; shit bit 0 into carry
 351+ E11C 30 08                                jr      nc,.SetKeyPressed               ; low bit means it was pressed
 352+ E11E FD 6F                                ld      iyl,a
 353+ E120                                      ZeroA
 353+ E120 AF          >                        xor a
 354+ E121 C3 2E E1                             jp      .SetKey
 355+ E124 20 0B                                jr		nz,.SkipKeySet
 356+ E126 FD 6F        .SetKeyPressed:	        ld      iyl,a                           ; save current input byte
 357+ E128 1A                                   ld      a,(de)                          ; get current keystate
 358+ E129 FE 02                                cp      2
 359+ E12B 28 02                                jr      z,.AlreadyHeld
 360+ E12D 3C                                   inc     a                               ; and increment by 1 as its moved from previous state
 361+ E12E 12           .SetKey:                ld		(de),a				  	        ; save key Pressed state
 362+ E12F FD 7D        .AlreadyHeld:           ld      a,iyl                           ; and retrieve the current input byte
 363+ E131 13           .SkipKeySet:	        inc		de								; move to next key
 364+ E132 10 E7                                djnz	.ProcessBitsLoop				; Process all key group bits
 365+ E134 0D                                   dec     c                               ; thats one row of bits all processed
 366+ E135 20 D9                                jr      nz,.PortReadLoop				; Read next input port
 367+ E137              .ReadExtend0:           ; bits are set to 1 for press on the next register
 368+ E137                                      GetNextReg EXTENDED_KEYS_0_REGISTER
 368+ E137 01 3B 24    >            ld bc,$243B
 368+ E13A 3E B0       >            ld a,EXTENDED_KEYS_0_REGISTER
 368+ E13C ED 79       >            out (c),a
 368+ E13E 04          >            inc b
 368+ E13F ED 78       >            in a,(c)
 369+ E141 32 40 E0                             ld      (RawKeys+8),a                   ; save to extended slot
 370+ E144 06 08                                ld      b,8
 371+ E146 21 28 E0                             ld      hl,Keys + VK_SEMI
 372+ E149 5F                                   ld      e,a                             ; e now holds the raw keys for shifting
 373+ E14A CB 13        .ProcessExtend0:        rl      e                               ; shift bits left into carry for extended keys
 374+ E14C 38 04                                jr      c,.SetExtend0KeyPressed         ; if carry they key was pressedw
 375+ E14E              .Extend0NotPressed:     ZeroA
 375+ E14E AF          >                        xor a
 376+ E14F C3 58 E1                             jp      .SetExtend0Key
 377+ E152 7E           .SetExtend0KeyPressed:  ld      a,(hl)                          ; consider if key was already held down
 378+ E153 FE 02                                cp      2
 379+ E155 28 02                                jr      z,.Extend0AlreadyHeld
 380+ E157 3C                                   inc     a
 381+ E158 77           .SetExtend0Key:         ld      (hl),a
 382+ E159 23           .Extend0AlreadyHeld:    inc     hl
 383+ E15A 10 EE                                djnz    .ProcessExtend0
 384+ E15C              .ReadExtend1:           GetNextReg EXTENDED_KEYS_1_REGISTER
 384+ E15C 01 3B 24    >            ld bc,$243B
 384+ E15F 3E B1       >            ld a,EXTENDED_KEYS_1_REGISTER
 384+ E161 ED 79       >            out (c),a
 384+ E163 04          >            inc b
 384+ E164 ED 78       >            in a,(c)
 385+ E166 32 41 E0                             ld      (RawKeys+9),a                      ; save to extended slot
 386+ E169 06 08                                ld      b,8
 387+ E16B 21 30 E0                             ld      hl,Keys + VK_DELETE
 388+ E16E 5F                                   ld      e,a
 389+ E16F CB 13        .ProcessExtend1:        rl      e                                 ; shift bits left into carry for extended keys
 390+ E171 38 04                                jr      c,.SetExtend1KeyPressed
 391+ E173              .Extend1NotPressed:     ZeroA
 391+ E173 AF          >                        xor a
 392+ E174 C3 7D E1                             jp      .SetExtend1Key
 393+ E177 7E           .SetExtend1KeyPressed:  ld      a,(hl)
 394+ E178 FE 02                                cp      2
 395+ E17A 28 02                                jr      z,.Extend1AlreadyHeld
 396+ E17C 3C                                   inc     a
 397+ E17D 77           .SetExtend1Key:         ld      (hl),a
 398+ E17E 23           .Extend1AlreadyHeld:    inc     hl
 399+ E17F 10 EE                                djnz    .ProcessExtend1
 400+ E181 C9                                   ret

 404+ E182              GetKeyStateAddressDE:   MACRO
 405+ E182 ~                                    ld      hl,KeyboardMap                  ; work our address to read from
 406+ E182 ~                                    add     hl,a
 407+ E182 ~                                    ld      e,(hl)
 408+ E182 ~                                    inc     hl
 409+ E182 ~                                    ld      d,(hl)                          ; now de = address in keypress list
 410+ E182                                      ENDM
